text: Flash cards of flash memory? Not quite. Here's what's actually going on. Every SSD is built on NAND flash cells, and TLC (triple-level cell) flash, the everyday workhorse in most drives, is good for roughly 3,000 write cycles per cell before it starts to wear out. That sounds limited, but the drive has a few tricks to get around it. Wear leveling spreads your writes evenly across every block, so no single cell gets overworked while its neighbors sit idle. Over-provisioning, typically around 7%, is a hidden reserve of spare flash that the controller uses to swap out worn blocks and keep performance steady. Together, these features stretch those 3,000 cycles across years of everyday use, so your drive can keep handling your photos, games, and work files reliably.
